environment: local Windows, python 3.12.10, torch 2.13.0+cpu (CPU-only), no CUDA usable locally
purpose: De-risk the real tabfm 1.0.0 + timesfm 2.0.2 call sequence and weight loading BEFORE building the GPU container. NOT the CUDA proof (that runs on the AWS T4 endpoint).

timesfm.cpu_result: OK: load 8.55s, forecast 1.16s; returns (point[1,h], quant[1,h,10]) = 10 quantile levels [mean,q0.1..q0.9]; real values e.g. [23.944, 23.247, 22.438, ...]
timesfm.device_handling: timesfm_2p5_torch auto-selects cuda:0 when torch.cuda.is_available() and moves inputs to model device (verified in package source) -> runs on the T4 automatically

tabfm.loader_bug: tabfm 1.0.0 load() hardcodes 'pytorch_model.bin' but the HF repo ships 'model.safetensors' -> load() raises FileNotFoundError. Workaround: construct TabFM(**ClassificationConfig().to_dict()) and load the published safetensors directly.
tabfm.weight_load: PASS: 913 tensors load into the real TabFM model with strict match (missing=0, unexpected=0) -> model + weights are genuine and architecturally exact
tabfm.safetensors_torch_note: safetensors.torch.load_file segfaults on THIS local torch 2.13.0+cpu build; safetensors.numpy.load_file works. The container uses a mainstream torch (>=2.0.0 satisfied by 2.5.x cu124); worker loads via safetensors.torch with a numpy fallback.
tabfm.predict_proba_cpu: hangs/pathologically slow on CPU (24-block ICL transformer, n_estimators ensemble) -> requires GPU; this is exactly why the workload runs on the T4, not on CPU/AppSail
tabfm.status: PASS for load+fit; predict requires GPU (by design)

conclusion: Both models are real, Apache-2.0, public, non-gated, and load correctly. TimesFM runs on CPU and auto-uses CUDA. TabFM loads exactly and must run on GPU. Proceed to build the GPU worker image (torch cu124) and prove real inference on the AWS T4 SageMaker async endpoint.
